item.title: A Balkan fairy tail
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article
Genre (Optional): Drama/Emotional, History

Page Layout (Optional): The article is made out of several camera and audio footages.

Elevator Pitch: The story is set in the Bosnian war. A girl with powers of a fairy is found in Bosnia. The Balkan MTF force captures her. Agent Kosta, an ethnic Croat born in Canada is sent to recover her but the Balkan base is atacked by the Chaos insurgency. The battle ends with Kosta and one insurgent as the only survivors. Kosta grabs the girl and they go through the war torn Bosnia, trying to reach the Croatian coast while runing from the still alive insurgent.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: As they drive through Bosnia, Kosta starts to bond with the kid. The child doesn't speak but communicates with Kosta by creating pictures on the various surfaces with her fairy dust. They meet various individuals from all three sides of the Bosnian conflict. In an abandoned coffy bar "Amsterdam", where all of the ethnicities laugh and drink together, while the girl, now going by the name Bojana Skadaric, plays with the other kids, he gets drunk and tells the sad fate of his wife, and how he lost her in a mission. His best friend Sam blamed him for her loss and they never saw each other again. The insurgent atacks the pub and destroys it. They reach an area controled by a Croatian warlord "Swedish" that commands a volunteer division while the local offical army unwillingly follows his orders. Swedish is in a blood feud with a local Serbian warlord. He finds out about the fairy abilities of the girl, as she intervened in an execution, but before he could capture her the Serbs start an offensive and the Serbian commander challenges Swedish to come out. Enraged, Swedish leads the volunteers to battle. The leader of the official army realises that his commander went completely insane, and orders the evacuation of the village. Kosta and Bojana go to the evacuation truck and is stoped by the voice of the chaos insurgent who calls Kosta by name, it is Sam. As he leaves to confront his former friend he tells the army leader to go far away with Bojana. He and Sam have only one bulet each and as they fire at each other a bomb drops between them, ending the footage.


Hook/Attention-Grabber: The story is about old conflicts that were never resolved coming to light. Bojana represents a generation not bound to those conflicts and has a future that she can choose freely, while Kosta, Sam and the people of Bosnia are chained to their fate.

item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes.

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: A set of twin beds that allow teleportation in between them. Sleeping in one bed will cause you to wake up in the other, regardless of distance between the two. The sleeper feels no change during the night, and cameras and surveillance of the bed during transport show the sleeper just vanishing.

Central Narrative: None.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: A bed used by the foundation to transport quickly across long distances.

Additional Notes: Not an extremely deep entry, but I just think it sounds good.

item.title: Cannibalism Cantaloupes - Seeking Greenlights
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout (Optional): In addition to the SCP and description an incident report with video log and an interview with someone present during the incident

Elevator Pitch: The SCP is a bunch of melon plants that compel people to eat them through a cognitohazard. Once they've been eaten a similar effect is placed on the head of the person who ate the melon, where other people will chase you to the ends of the earth in order to eat your brains, nose, eyes and all that good stuff.
Edit: The effect does not transfer to those who ate the infected person, but a new plant wil grow out of their skull after a couple weeks, killing them in the process.

Central Narrative: One of the members of the team that went to retrieve the SCP was pulled in by its effect and then eaten by the rest of their team members. The video log in the incident report and interview will show two perspectives on the horrors that unfolded, with the log showing an objective perspective and the interview a hazy and traumatized perspective.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: It's very much inspired by zombie stories, at least the part where your friends become the monsters you have to fight.

Additional Notes: I'm new to writing these articles and don't know every object on the site, so I don't know if this sort of stuff is something that's been done to death

item.title: Idea: Intertemporal Boots (Stay With Me Here)
item.content:encoded:
The SCP is a pair of boots. They would either be made from cloth and have a magical 'Serpent's Hand' sort of feel, or be completely robotic/futuristic. The file would go over the basic mechanics of the boots and testing would include D-Class being thrown throughout various time periods only to have the Foundation return them via some sort of temporal anchor.

Nothing crazy at first, walking forward on the x and z axis causes the user to jump forward in time. Walking backward on the x and z-axis causes them to jump backward in time. The file should get weirder when the D-Class starts moving on the y-axis. This segment would be heavily redacted/classified, but I think the file should imply that the D-Class is visiting other timelines that lay parallel to our own. (It's this part were I would need the most help on brainstorming ideas.)

Just an idea, but it would be a real hoot to write. I'm aiming for more of a Series I/II feel with this article. Nothing world-ending about this SCP, just some anomalous dimension shifting.


Forum category: Writing Help / Help: Ideas Critique
Forum thread: Idea: Intertemporal Boots (Stay With Me Here)

I feel like this piece couldn't decide between being about the characters, or about the foundation responding to a temporal collapse, and rather than take the best of both worlds ended up in a space where neither really shined.

The levity of the footnotes takes away from the gravity of the situation rather than emphasizing it. Like, I can appreciate that sort of "well, it's the end of the world I guess" tone, but it doesn't work well in contrast to a very rigid clinical tone. If you wanted this to be a piece that focusses more on the characters, I would want to give them more space to breathe and develop so we can feel actual attachment to them.

If this piece was more supposed to be about the foundation's reaction as a whole, I would do away with the footnotes and make the conprocs tell a more detailed and nuanced story of what the foundation considers valuable. Right now the conprocs feel a little bland in terms of "things the foundation would do". It leaves a lot up to generalization and abstraction rather than zeroing on particularly evocative details.

I also really don't think the listpages was effective here. Like, you could've just let the article end on the first page and I think you would've gotten the point across. The refresh button and next page artificially lengthens the piece. While sure, the piece isn't that long to begin with, that does make any additional length much more noticeable. If you're going for short, you really need to make sure you're making every word count, and most of the words on the new page are just a rehash of a memo on the previous page.

Overall, I think if this wants to be about the end of the world, it would be better to decide what part of the end of the world you want to actually focus on.

-1

One of the SCPs I am currently planning to write is a high-powered thaumaturgist (named Quinn), and he was killed in an alternate universe. The GoC and Horizon Initiative (horizon initiative because he has ties to a religious organization that worships deities of magic) breached Quinn's containment and killed him before Nine Tail Fox could intervene and eliminate the invading GoC and HI soldiers. After that, he went to corbenic, and, since he was actually a good-aligned human who didn't do anything immoral, he didn't get punished. He immediately realized that his thaumaturgist powers worked in this afterlife, and that he could even summon his cat familiar still.

After that, he slowly started to realized that the Three Moons Initiatives' leader (or more like leaders) are kinda tyrannical dictators, and many shared that sentiment. He managed to effectively cancel out their deity's powers with an anti-magic fields (see high-powered thaumaturgist), and even managed to create stuff similar to Scranton Realist Anchors, rendering all anomalous abilities and weaponry. He also destroyed a lot of military weapons and equipment in the process, and stole what he could for his fellow revolters.

I plan to mention these events in a seperate SCP, as well as in a tale. The SCP entry given basics and scraps of info, while the tale would basically be an "explanation" entry.

item.title: Re: It Will Not Leave
item.content:encoded:
This…is a really strong newbie concept.

Okay. Warning. Rambley crit ahead. So please.

+Bear with me
-Yeet

I adore the emotional aspect and I'm a sucker for…how should I put it? 'Dead spirit super attached to living person' stories? Best way to put it?

I do have issues, though. First off…the topic of suicide. It's a difficult topic to handle, as it's extremely sensitive and one needs to pull it off well in order to make it work. I really like what you have here in concept, but I'm worried about the execution.

Also, go here
http://www.scpwiki.com/task-forces#omega-0

And look at the Mobile Task Force called MTF Omega-0 ("Ará Orún"). In summary, it's a Mobile Task Force comprised of the spirits(?) of dead Foundation personnel.

Note: SCP Foundation storytelling is allheadcanon, so you don't have to do anything with this MTF, but I figured someone would mention it later down the road, so I figured you'd need to know.

Also, I get it's just a hallucination and not actually a spirit, but still. I just wanted to share that MTF.

My last question is this: tell me why this needs to be an SCP and not a Tale.

A Tale, you have so much freedom to tell a story however you choose.

An SCP with its restrictive post-mortem emotionless scientific document format, the best way I can see this being told is a combination of interviews, handwritten notes, video footage of the MTFs behavior, perhaps some examples of on the field mission logs where the grieving MTF soldier starts losing his cool and goes nuts. That can all work perfectly, I admit but I'd want to see how you'd portray it.

In a Tale, you can accurately describe everything down to the nitty gritty of the MTF seeing his dead mate and such.

In the SCP format, all you'd be showing is someone going nuts from an outsider's perspective. The only anomalous bit would be the kicker in an addendum that someone else started hallucinating it.

Both have their strengths but I just want you to be aware of what storytelling tools you have.

Now, one final issue I have. This is a grave one. Extremely grave issue.

In benefit of maintaining resources, rather than promoting an adequate mental health, Foundation classifies it as an anomaly and moves on.

I don't see money as an issue to the Foundation. Also, this person's Mobile Task Force. I don't really buy them just shrugging him off like that.

The 'not an anomaly but emotions turn it into an anomaly' bit, I see working just fine. If anything, this can toy with the reader's expectations and make them wonder whether it really is a ghost or just a hallucination.

The careless attitude of the Foundation, I don't buy. Besides, I imagine they have on site mental health experts.

I don't know, maybe have him be checked out repeatedly by mental health experts and then have it fail and then have it be classified as an anomaly afterwards? After he commits suicide (which you'll still need to find a way to execute well.)

Simply saying 'screw it' and classifying an anomaly out of desire to save funds is so not Foundation.

Anywho, that ends my incredibly rambley crit. I apologise if some of this was a little unclear. If you need clarification, feel free to PM me.

I hope I helped and I bid you a lovely day.

👍


Forum category: Writing Help / Help: Ideas Critique
Forum thread: It Will Not Leave

This article isn’t technically bad, but it’s bland and that might be worse. SZ and AF are barely characters; their dialogue is spartan and only tells us that they’ve worked together before. Both the disaster and the buildup feel underwhelming because the CK class shift is never expounded upon and the containment procedures don’t do a good job of demonstrating the escalating scale of the threat. The ending is similarly predictable — the timeline was wiped out but I don’t feel any sense of loss because I barely knew it. There’s a lot of similarities here at the idea level to SCP-2317 and Lily’s Proposal, but the former actually escalates the threat and thus intrigue of the anomaly and the latter actively creates a melancholy tone that sells the poignancy of its core idea. 5618, in comparison, lays out a threat but fails to make the escalation feel meaningful or convey the poignancy of the end of the world.

item.title: Re: SCP Idea - A house and its occupant
item.content:encoded:
Hi! Thanks for the crit.

+ show block
– hide block

I totally understand what you mean. I spent a couple days on IRC asking around for some help on this piece, and people kept telling me that it needed either more story, more of a personal connection with XXXX-A (because she's human), or both. I tried to do both, but I am really bad at explaining things.

My goal isn't to entirely tell the story of the SCP just using the first person, where XXXX-A is speaking the entire time; rather, I want to write in the first person to evolve XXXX-A as more than just 'one more SCP to contain', and give XXXX-A a bit of personality and connection.

My goal for the tests she performs with the Foundation are SCP-XXXX specific, and with Foundation goals in mind, such as how can XXXX-A's abilities be exploited to benefit the Foundation (can she summon things that can provide energy? Can she summon weapons? Foundation-critical resources?)

Additionally, I didn't want to really make this SCP one full of conflict, but I do agree that there should be more tension. I wanted to portray a softer side of the Foundation, in which this SCP cooperates with the Foundation, and they don't enforce harsh containment restrictions upon her because of her attitude towards the Foundation.

item.title: Re: A parallel world
item.content:encoded:
+ show block
– hide block

Why do these exist? Like did someone make them and how?

I currently don't explain why they exist, although the shape of them being a gear (on the parallel world side) hints towards them being some sort of ancient machinery (whether this extracted energy from the parallel world or something else is also not explained right now).

More to the point, what does experiencing it and investigating it through them look like?

I'm not sure I understand the question. By performing experiments on how the artifacts move, we deduce the presence of a fluid in the other world. By how they move on their own we also deduce that there are weather-like events in the other world. By measuring temperature we can take guesses at the temperature in the other world etc. Is that what you mean?

How do they allow this to happen?

You mean how the creators of the artifact allow this? They are long dead.

the parallel worlds existence should matter for some reason within this narrative so that what it is like is important to a reader; and it feels to me that it's…too emotionally distant?

The current connections to our world seem to be that a 28 days cycle in the temperatures of the parallel world, hinting at some relation to our lunar cycle. And a 24 hour cycle on the sound activity of the parallel world, hinting at some relation to the Earth's rotation.

I could perhaps elaborate more and add more connections to our world. Perhaps the artifacts were discovered near some other pieces that look like they were part of a power generator for some machinery that was used in some ancient battle. Or perhaps they were discovered with parts that hint on them being used by someone on the parallel world that was trying to harvest energy from our world (think of a wind turbine that takes kinetic energy to the parallel world).

And from these consequences, a story should evolve: they should provide tension and allow you to introduce a beginning/middle/end and stuff and like…closure as the consequences are in some way wrapped up, y'know?

Is it standard/common for SCPs to have a story? I thought that many were more like lab reports, not necessarily telling a big story with a few incident reports in there (which I do have a few of in my draft) I don't have anything against having a big story but I would like to keep it more archeological though, perhaps the story should be in the past and told through ancient texts instead of it happening inside the foundation? Perhaps an ancient story about how contact was made with a civilization in the parallel world, and how they cooperated with us to create these energy generators in exchange for something. Maybe a story about them becoming hostile in the process and eventually the earthlings breaking apart the machinery to cut them off?

Thanks for the ideas!

Hello there, tordzak. Welcome to the SCP Wiki!

If you're interested in horror, history, and all that, I recommend you check out our IRC chatrooms. There, you can talk with people from the community about a wide variety of topics. Not only that, but you can make some great friends on there. If you do decide to join and you have troubles connecting, feel free to ask for help in the #site17 channel. Anyways, here's some stuff you may want to check out when getting started:

Navigation:

+ show block
– hide block

If you want to keep up with the latest material, check out the Most Recently Created page. If you'd rather check out only the most popular new articles, then Top Rated New Pages is the way to go.

While you're browsing, if you find an article you absolutely love, you can try finding more from the same author by looking them up on the Authors' Page hub. If the user in question is not on that list, you can try searching for them on our statistic site, scpper.com.

If there are some SCPs that you're a fan of, you can try checking out a new addition to the wiki: the SCP Series Tales List, created by yours truly. These are pages that mirror the main SCP listings, but they include all the stories that feature each SCP (for example, one can find everything that has been written about SCP-173).

Recommendations:

+ show block
– hide block

With the amount of SCPs we have, it can be hard to find really good articles in specific genres (not to mention we have no way of searching by genre), so I took it upon myself to curate a few lists of some good representative material to share with other users. With the help of various community members, User-Curated Lists has been built to facilitate fun wikiwalks of some amazing content!

With that said, I hope you enjoy your time here.
